items.strategy: For nonempty compact Hausdorff K over R or C, the extreme points of the dual ball are exactly c delta_x, |c|=1. items.statement: For Tychonoff X the following are equivalent: C_p(X) is Frechet-Urysohn; it is sequential; it is a k-space; X has the gamma-property. An omega-cover is an open cover not containing X such that every finite subset is contained in a member; a gamma-cover is infinite and each point belongs to all but finitely many members; the gamma-property requires each open omega-cover to contain a gamma-subcover. Recorded only; no selection-principle theorem is used in the Gelfand proofs.

items.strategy: State norm identity, linearity, multiplicativity, conjugation, and uniform convergence; real-valued functions give self-adjoint operators. For f>=0, first write f(T)=g(T)*g(T) with g=sqrt(f) as a scalar continuous function, so positivity uses quadratic forms without an operator square-root theorem. Conversely positive f(T) has nonnegative spectrum by the earlier lemma. For continuous g on f(sigma T), prove g(f(T))=(g composed f)(T) first for *-polynomials, then uniformly. Add functoriality for unital *-maps and consistency with holomorphic calculus only after verifying its contour supplier; this remains an explicit blocked seam. The calculus commutes with every operator commuting with self-adjoint T; for normal T require commutation with both T and T* unless a separate Fuglede theorem is proved.
